title: Delhi High Court Denies Bail to Red Fort Blast 'In-House Engineer' Jasir Wani
excerpt: The court rejected a default bail plea by the accused, who allegedly modified drones, built rocket IEDs, and used AI tools to aid the November 2025 terror attack that killed 11 people.
body:
• The Delhi High Court denied default bail to Jasir Bilal Wani, a 20-year-old accused described by the NIA as the "in-house engineer" of the terror module behind the November 2025 Red Fort car bomb blast.
  • The NIA's 7,500-page chargesheet alleges Wani modified drones, fabricated rocket IEDs, and used ChatGPT and YouTube to research explosive devices for the Al-Qaeda-linked group.
  • Thirteen people have been chargesheeted so far in the case, which exposed a "white-collar" terror network of doctors and professionals linked to Al-Qaeda in the Indian Subcontinent.

The Delhi High Court has denied a default bail application filed by Jasir Bilal Wani, a key accused in the November 10, 2025, car bomb blast near Delhi's Red Fort that killed 11 people and injured several others. Wani, described by the National Investigation Agency as the terror module's "in-house engineer," has been in custody since his arrest on November 17, 2025.

The court's decision keeps Wani behind bars as the NIA continues its prosecution under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, which imposes stringent conditions for granting bail in terrorism cases.

The Red Fort Attack

On November 10, 2025, a vehicle-borne improvised explosive device detonated near the Red Fort in Delhi, killing 11 people and causing extensive damage to the surrounding area. The driver of the explosive-laden car, Dr. Umar Un Nabi, a former assistant professor at Al Falah University in Faridabad, died in the blast.

https://x.com/timesofindia/status/2089842274163458445

The attack was carried out by an interim terror module of Ansar Ghazwat-ul-Hind, an offshoot of Al-Qaeda in the Indian Subcontinent. The NIA described the operation as a meticulously planned "white-collar" terror conspiracy involving radicalised medical professionals and technical operatives.

Wani's Alleged Role

The NIA's 7,500-page chargesheet, filed in May 2026 before a special court in New Delhi, details Wani's alleged role as the group's technical backbone. According to the agency, the 20-year-old BSc student from Qazigund in Anantnag district, Jammu and Kashmir, provided critical support on multiple fronts.

Investigators allege Wani modified drones supplied by Dr. Nabi, improving their flying range and payload capacity with the aim of weaponising them for attacks on security installations. He allegedly fabricated and tested rocket IEDs in the forests of Qazigund, with remnants later recovered by NIA teams.

"The accused had turned to YouTube and ChatGPT, searching for 'how to make a rocket and in what proportion should the mixture be.'"

— NIA chargesheet, May 2026

The chargesheet further reveals that between December 2023 and January 2024, Wani ordered components for trigger mechanisms through his Flipkart account — including a proximity switch, radio frequency transmitter-receiver kit, soldering equipment, and other electronics — funded by Dr. Nabi. These components were allegedly assembled into the trigger mechanism that detonated the vehicle-borne IED.

The explosive used in the blast was triacetone triperoxide (TATP), which the accused reportedly manufactured after experiments to perfect the mixture.

The Wider Conspiracy

Thirteen people have been chargesheeted in connection with the blast. Besides Wani, the accused include key conspirator Amir Rashid Ali, doctors Muzammil Ganaie, Adeel Rather, and Shaheena Saeed — all employed at Al Falah University — and preacher Maulvi Irfan Ahmed Wagay. A supplementary chargesheet filed in June 2026 added three more names, including an absconding paediatrician identified as a founding member of the AGuH interim module.

The case has drawn attention for the professional backgrounds of the accused, with the NIA dubbing it a "white-collar" terror plot. Al Falah University in Faridabad came under scrutiny after the investigation revealed that three doctors employed there were directly involved in the conspiracy.

Legal Proceedings Under UAPA

Under Section 43D(5) of UAPA, courts cannot grant bail if, on a prima facie assessment, the accusations appear to be true. This provision makes obtaining bail in terrorism cases exceptionally difficult, and courts have consistently upheld its constitutionality.

The Delhi High Court's denial of Wani's default bail application is in line with this framework. The court had earlier also rejected Wani's plea to meet his lawyer at the NIA headquarters, with Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma remarking that he was "not a special person" and that standard procedures must be followed.

What Comes Next

The trial is expected to proceed before the special NIA court at Patiala House Courts in New Delhi. The NIA continues to coordinate with police agencies across multiple states, pursuing leads to identify any remaining members of the network. The investigation has revealed the use of AI platforms and commercially available materials in terror planning — a dimension that security agencies are watching closely.
